Hold a celebration and banquet on New Earth to celebrate the completion of the terraforming project.
Terraforming
The atmosphere must be safe; if it is not, wait for your scientists to stabilise it
This feast is so elaborate to prepare, it can be attempted only once per turn.
You prepare a holographic proclamation announcing New Earth to the cosmos

“A new Eden, like in the time of Ancients, this world will nurture humanity.”

You also draft invitations for the triumphal feast. Now, who to invite to this auspicious gathering?
the terraforming of New Earth

You announce that the festivities will continue at a second location, away from the main space station

“Our shuttles will convey you there.”

The guests exchange quizzical glances. Why leave the comfort of the station? Confused, they board the vessels.
The shuttles land on the surface of New Earth

On a wide, flat clearing beside a blue lake, your guests are surprised to find a dozen banquet tables laden with sweetmeats. An open banquet hall - more a courtyard - has been erected here: the tables, even the food, are exposed to the elements.

“Is this some kind of trick?” one cries. “Are you trying to kill us?” The guests huddle into their spacesuits.

But they soon notice the sun’s warmth through their visors.
The placid lake, dotted with algae and plant life.
You clamber onto your shuttle and address the crowd via suit radio

“For the first time in centuries, human beings will eat and drink under a blue sky, with the breeze in their hair. We have spent too long shut in our sterile cages. This is how we are meant to be.” 

You pour yourself a goblet of wine. The bottle feels coarse through the spacesuit glove; the wine is murky through your helmet.
Remove your helmet
You unhook your collar clasps; the crowd gasp as you pull off the helmet
You take a few deep breaths. The air feels crisp.
Braved terraformed atmosphere
You pluck the goblet from the table and take a sip. It’s the sweetest wine you ever tasted.
Terraforming esteem
Too crisp: you gasp for air, cramming the helmet back on. Your guests sneer: this terraforming business was a fool’s dream after all.
Terraforming failure
Order a servant to remove his helmet first
The servant unhooks his collar clasps; the crowd gasp as he removes the helmet
He takes a few shallow breaths. You see fear in his eyes, as though he mistrusts his own lungs.

After a moment, he takes the goblet and presents it to you on a platter. “Would my liege try the vintage?”

You unclasp your helmet and take a sip. “Your liege would.”
Terraforming esteem

His eyes bulge and redden, his breath rasping. He falls to the floor, gasping, and his breathing slows.

Your guests sneer: this terraforming business was a fool’s dream after all.
Terraforming failure
The nearby wood, filled with buzzing insects and twittering birds.
Slowly, your guests shed their spacesuits
Soon they are eating, talking, laughing. They pour water on the ground and marvel as the earth soaks it up. They swim in the lake, splashing each other mischievously.
They chase each other through the trees, shrieking.
You take a moment to appreciate your world, and the rivals and allies you have brought together here.

Praised terraforming
The day draws on; shadows lengthen

Your guests are treated to a breathtaking sight: their first true sunset. “As though the cosmos itself welcomes us,” {d(RandomGuest)} whispers.

Night draws in. Your entourage pack up the banquet and return to the station, where the feast can continue in warmth and comfort. Your guests do not want to leave.
You summon {HostingHouse}’s scientists, brow knit with fury

“What went wrong?” you bellow. “That atmosphere should be breathable!”

They shuffle their feet; something about a toxic chain reaction, an imbalance in planetary humours. They assure you the problem will be fixed soon.

“It had better,” you growl. “{HostingHouse} must make up for this embarrassment. Only a second gathering could rectify our guests' doubts...”
Terraforming feast ruined
While the guests settle down for the night at the station, you take a shuttle back to New Earth

Strolling along the lakeside, you fix the feast in your memory. People will speak of this day for centuries.

You sit on the ground; breathe deeply; feel the breeze on your face.
Weeds waft gently in the lake water.
You hear a rustle in the undergrowth: a small mammal? The scene is shrouded in a gentle insect buzz, and the calls of birdsong.
It could be a bright summer day on old Earth.

One hundred years after the New Earth Banquet, the rulers of the cosmos gather at the capital city, New {HomeSystem}
“The achievement of {PlayerHouse} cannot be overstated,” the Commissioner cries in her opening address.

“We were in darkness. New Earth became a beacon guiding us home - at first a barren waste, but slowly made to bloom. This world has at last flourished, blessed with creatures of all kinds over the past century. 

“In recognition of this, it is my privilege to crown Archon {lastName(PlayerCharacter)}, grandchild of the great {PlayerCharacter}, in the sight of all rulers of the galaxy, as our supreme Emperor.”
The crown settles on your head
It is heavy. Elaborate. Wrought from shipwright Viridium from each ruler’s fleet, the gems given freely from each ruler’s private collection.
{PlayerCharacter} reforged a planet, an eternal haven for your people, and led them home.
You stand, ready to address them as Emperor, eager to lead them now into the future.
